summary: Root-caused and replaced the earlier negative reachability result. The superseded five-node harness cut only the leader↔majority links, leaving partner↔majority open, so the partner was never isolated: it took the successor's entries during the partition and was already repaired before the heal, which is exactly why it converged with zero restores. With the partition sealed on both sides, the same legal history keeps its shape and the loop appears: divergent_prefix {base_index 2, partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 1..7} shows the precondition produced by the partitioned leader's own AppendEntries; successor_snapshot {snapshot_index 4, successor_store 0/0} shows full compaction; rejoin_observe {restores_before 0, restores_early 694, restores_late 705, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 7, successor_applied_index 4, successor_commit_index 4} shows the partner installing the same snapshot ~700 times in the ~1.3 s window with its advertised last index stuck at 7 and its applied index pinned at the snapshot index. That answers the two open gaps (the peer was reconciled only because it was never isolated; the successor supplied the entries over the still-open link) and withdraws the earlier narrowing of the leader-side loop as an artifact — the non-progress/snapshot-resend cycle is now reproduced on a produced five-node history, not just the seeded single-peer one. Recorded as a standalone correction Fact (the superseded entries live in earlier batches and their ids are not resolvable here, so the correction names them in prose with changed premise and affected objects), plus a successor experiment with the two-sided partition so the controller can retain the receipt; the interpretation stays conclusion=unresolved / defect_claim=unresolved because this batch cannot link a receipt to a fixed experiment. Structural validation returned valid=true.
